$note: Every off-band CLAIM the four parcel generators would make, named with the reason it stands. Cut by tools/measure_family_deal.py --write-baseline; read by --gate as a RATCHET, the same shape tools/band_claims_baseline.json uses for the records that landed. A refusal is never baselined — a family a parcel may deal and the archetype will not build is a run that dies, and all four parcels are green on that today. What is baselined is the second assertion: a value outside the band its own note cites is wrong about its source (K25). The fault may shrink and may not grow.
$measured: 2026-08-28, T-0172. 400 synthetic deals per family per parcel. 0 refusals across all four parcels; 31 off-band claims on 25 (parcel, family) rows, every one a per-family CONSTANT, so each is made on 100 per cent of that family's deals. 12 of the 15 (family, field) pairs behind them already stand as landed offenders in band_claims_baseline.json; three do NOT — west H2 eave, west H2 pitch and household H1 eave — and those are the latent shape this sweep exists to catch, a card the recipe may deal and has not.

$repairs.$why: The repair is one shape in all three files and it is not an edit: replace the literal with family_bands.pitch_deg / wall_height_m sampled inside the family's own band and bounded by eave_limits, which is exactly what T-0144 and T-0145 did to the platted-block parcel. It moves the eave and the pitch on every standing record of those families, so it re-derives and re-bakes. One ticket per parcel because one bake per parcel is what a run holds.
